disposition_reason: As, Cd, Pb, Cu and Zn were measured by AAS in 36 samples of 12 meat, meat product, soup concentrate and fish foods; every sample value is printed in Tables 1 to 6.

study.design: Small market basket survey of foods for a full-day military meal; three units per food from different manufacturers or suppliers
study.origin: Macedonian region producers; fish and sardine from producers in the wider region
study.market: purchased for the Military Medical Center, Skopje, North Macedonia
study.method: Wet digestion with nitric acid; flame AAS (Cu, Zn), hydride generation AAS (As), graphite furnace AAS (Cd, Pb)
lod: Cu 0.4, Zn 0.5, As 0.5, Cd 0.1, Pb 0.6 (printed 'g/L', read as µg/L in solution)
study.qa: No CRM, recovery or replicate data reported

unresolved: Detection limits are printed as 'g/L'; the micro sign appears lost, so read as µg/L in solution.
Wet or dry basis not stated.
Canned meat cuts lead (440 to 508 µg/kg) is above the EU maximum level for meat of 100 µg/kg, although the authors call all values below the national limits; limits are not printed.
Zinc values (0.3 to 8 mg/kg) are low for meat and fish; possible unit issue not resolvable from the text.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Maximum levels, Rulebook on general requirements for food safety, Official Gazette of RM no. 102/2013
regulatory_or_exposure.value: authors state all samples were below the maximum allowable levels; limits not printed
